Waddup people I'm Unpronounceable and I am the mod for this subverse. This subverse is aiming to be like the sub of the same name from "that other place".

In other words it is a subverse for requesting and suggesting anime and anime related media. What counts as anime related? The current accepted media is:

  • Anime

  • Anime inspired shows/movies

  • Manga

  • Light Novels

  • Visual Novels

The rules are all in the sidebar but I'm gonna write em' up here in a little more dietail,

1. Spoilers are not allowed. This one is a given, of course you shouldn't spoil an anime you're trying to recommend. If it is crucial to your recommendation to spoil something then use spoiler tags. Sometimes people post requests that are basically asking for spoilers, example: "Anime where the MC dies at the end." In these kind of threads you have to put the name of the anime in spoiler tags.

2. All post must use the appropriate flairs. The flairs are:

  • Request - Used for anime request i.e "Long running battle shounen that''s not the big three"

  • Suggestion - Used for suggesting an anime i.e "Like romance and action? Then watch X"

  • Manga/LN/VN - Used for Suggesting or Requesting Manga, Light Novels or Visual Novels

  • Question - Used if you have a related question such as "In what order should I watch X anime?"

  • Identification - Used for when you don't have the name of a certain hentai but you can describe it good enough for someone to recognize it

So apparently only mods can flair posts. So I'll be doing it untill that's fixed. So you don't have to worry about this rule. Yet...

4. Search before you post. Chances are a similar request or the same suggestion has already been made.

5. No hentai. There is /v/hentaisuggest for that. Ecchi does not count as hentai though.

6. Post about why you should not watch a show are not allowed. So no "Don't watch this piece of shit anime"

Convince me on why I should ditch Windows(7/Free upgrade) to 10 for Linux when I game/stream/record/etc.
Convince me on why I should convince you.

To be honest, right now Windows is still superiour for gaming and streaming. Sure, there are a lot of games, and it's coming along, especially with SteamOS coming up, and there is OBS for Linux as well. But overall, if your main interest is having a computer that just works for gaming, Windows might be the better choice for you.

With that being said, I personally think Linux (and *nix in general) is vastly superiour in many aspects (better overall quality, more secure, no NSA backdoors, no corp trying to make profit off you, etc), and if you are willing to do work and especially learn, you can certainly make the switch. There will be downsides, things will most likely break, things might not work at all, but the community is really nice and helpful, and if you want to, you can make it happen. But you have to want it yourself, otherwise there is no point to it. I like promoting live-sticks for this cause. Inform yourself what kind of distributions are newbie-friendy and looks interesting to you and try it from a stick. Performance will be worse, but you can play around with it, touch stuff, break stuff and see if this is an experience you would like to have, all without any risk.

You would have the opportunity to get used to Linux before it gets "hot", so you would be able to show-off your tux skills to people when Linux has Android'd both the Console and PC markets. Linux already has more games than the ps3. Not the ps4, which is just as young as Linux when it comes to the gaming world, but the veteran that is the ps3. It becomes funny when you read news saying how badly Microsoft messed up on something and their "Features" aren't forced down your throat anymore. Also, like @sulami said, you don't have to worry anymore about backdoors and corporations.
Oh and, the installation should actually be easier than the Windows one. Quicker, too.
On top of all this, you don't even have to replace Windows. Many Linux users keep Windows on the side for specific software and games.
Though GPU performance might be inferior to Windows for now, things will change soon. People will want to buy the best Steam Machine, and the best one will have a GPU with the best support/drivers and the drivers really are the biggest problem one can face when gaming on Linux for now. Especially with AMD hardware, sadly. (I still game on my AMD laptop!)
